name: daydreaming
description: Allowing your experience to wander through thoughts perceived as more pleasant than your actual situation.
perceptions: It's more pleasant to imagine other things.
results: Perhaps time passes more enjoyably, or perhaps time gets away from you.

guidance.description: Perhaps day dreaming is something that should be encouraged.
We all have times when we really want to daydream but shouldn’t.

variations.name: zoning out
variations.description: Unintentionally falling into a state that lacks focus, often negatively impacting something you're supposed to be doing.
perceptions: What I'm supposed to be doing is not holding my attention.
It's difficult to focus on my actual situation.
examples: Difficulty focusing while working on a project.

guidance.description: Zoning out is a mild and common form of dissociation. It can serve as a coping mechanism when you’re bored, stressed, or dealing with a difficulty in your life.
guidance.attribution: Crystal Raypole and Timothy J. Legg, PhD, PsyD

variations.name: negative daydreaming
variations.description: Your thoughts are pulled in ways that are perceived as less pleasant than your actual situation.
perceptions: Something negative is pulling my attention.
It's difficult to focus on my actual situation.
results: Perhaps you'll find an angle to resolve a negative situation, but you may just sustain your anxiety.
examples: Simmering on how your ex treated you.

guidance.description: While occasional mind-wandering is common, when these daydreams become prolonged or delusional they can affect your mental and even physical health.

comparisons.description: Imagination is the general capacity to mentally experience something that you have't experienced in real life before. Daydreaming often includes a stream of imaginative thoughts, but sometimes it centers on reliving experiences.

commentaries.quote: It is better to be lost in a beautiful daydream than trapped in a dim reality.
That daydreaming mode turns out to be restorative. It's like hitting the reset button in your brain.
I'm often daydreaming, and it's because I've always liked the idea of there being something more than the normal world.
If you aren't focused on what's right here in front of you, if you're daydreaming about what might be, you really aren't focused at all.

A daydream is a meal at which images are eaten. Some of us are gourmets, some gourmands, and a good many take their images precooked out of a can and swallow them down whole, absent-mindedly and with little relish.
